articleTitle: Signal Integrity and Power Integrity Challenges in Embedded Computing Boards
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The demand for smaller size, lesser weight, lower power, higher performance and faster speed has set the trend for multi-threaded and multi-core CPU based embedded design. Such design are associated with various challenges which includes space constraints, trace routing constraints, length matching, signal integrity, power integrity, EMI/EMC constraints and thermal management. Systematic design approach and simulations helps to address these challenges in the design stage itself thereby reducing the time to market. The purpose of this paper is to analyze the various design challenges in High Speed embedded systems, related to Signal Integrity (SI) and Power Integrity (PI) and the practical solutions to overcome these challenges.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Analysis of Complementary FSS for Selective EM Shielding
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, an array of complementary periodic Jerusalem cross FSS element has been discussed for effective electromagnetic (EM) shielding application. A simple equivalent circuit (EC) in conjunction with transmission line (TL) model is used to analyze the response of two closely coupled complementary conducting elements printed on either side of the substrate. The described EC method can predict the scattering parameters with high accuracy. Further, an extensive parametric study of CFSS is performed to analyze its frequency response. The CFSS exhibits a highly stable response with two controllable passbands for normal and oblique incidences. Such response is more suitable for allowing two bands with strong stopband between them.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Octagonal Shaped Patch Antenna With Slits For Dual-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, an octagonal shaped patch (OSP) antenna with co-planar waveguide feed is presented. The proposed antenna is operates at two frequency bands with a below -10dB reflection coefficient. The first frequency band is operates 9.8 to 11.6GHz with -24.6dB reflection coefficient at 10.6GHz resonating frequency, whereas the second band is operates 14 to 21.9GHz with -30dB reflection coefficient at 18.6GHz resonating frequency. The simulation results show that, the proposed antenna operates at dual band frequencies with impedance bandwidths 1.8 and 7.9 GHz respectively. The gain is observed 5.25 dBi and 4.67 dBi at respective frequencies.

articleTitle: Modeling, Simulation & Validation of TEM Cell for Short Pulse Sensor Verification
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The Transverse Electro-Magnetic (TEM) cell is popular among EMI/EMC community ever since its invention. Its versatility in radiated susceptibility tests as well as in measuring radiated emissions from a product.In this paper, open TEM cell was modeled using CST and analyzed it for pulsed signals viz. Square and Double Exponential type. RS105, EMP pulse characteristics were also studied and analyzed using modeled TEM cell. Practical measurements were carried out using similar available TEM cell in our laboratory and results concurrence with simulated results for square type pulse. Modeled TEM cell will be used for pulsed E-filed sensors verification and also for RS105 testing of smaller objects based on uniform field results obtained in simulation using double exponential pulse excitation.

articleTitle: Experimental approach to identify source of radiation noise over Si and SiC power modules
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Continually dynamic characteristics of semiconductor power chips (say chips) for inverter use have been studied and improved to reduce loss and to downsize chip area, but it implies that radiation noise has been increasing. This paper shows one of experimental approach to identify source of radiation noise over inverter system with power device by visualizing near field magnetic field and FFT processed noise voltage from antenna with comparing two devices installing all Si chips and all SiC chips.

articleTitle: A Paper Based Perfect Electromagnetic Wave Absorber Using Conducting Grid Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: A paper based simple, flexible, and perfect resonant electromagnetic wave absorber is proposed in this article. The absorber consists of the conducting grid patterns where unit cell of the pattern is a two-dimensional grid based structure and the bottom is a conducting ground plane. The grid based top conducting patterns are created by inkjet printing over a thin paper having conducting layer at the bottom. The proposed absorber undoubtedly attains a cost-effective and eco-friendly solution for designing a flexible electromagnetic absorber. The experimental and simulation results are found to be in excellent agreement. The proposed absorber exhibits perfect absorption of 99.99% at 10.84 GHz and possesses an overall thickness of 0.531 mm.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Mechanically Stirred Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, a Mechanically Stirred Reverberation chamber situated at Electronics and Radar Development Establishment (LRDE) has been studied and its performance has been analyzed in accordance with the performance indicators specified by IEC 61000:21-4 standard. Electromagnetic Simulation has been performed on the 3D Model of the Reverberation Chamber using CST Microwave Studio, and the simulation results obtained have been found to closely approximate the practical measurement results.

articleTitle: Study on Modeling & Simulation Analysis of Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Coupling to Cables
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) analysis has become a serious concern in design to production cycle of the electronics in the last decade. EMP poses a severe threat to the communication lines, power grids, RF links etc. The EMP coupling analysis needs to be carried out to address the severity of the pulse coupled and to provide mitigation guidelines. A study on modeling of cables and cable penetration to shelter is carried out and simulated for coupling of EMP into it. Altair HyperWorks FEKO Simulation tool is used to analyze the currents generated at the cable ports & penetrations. The generated currents are compared for the coupling levels obtained for the cables.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Near Field Emission from the PCB of a Car Deck Player
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The advanced system in an automobile tends to incorporate within a confined space to save some place inside the automobile. However, the components interfere with each other, which produces EMI related problems. Hence, to overcome such EMI associated glitches, it is necessary to carry out an investigation and a detailed EMI/EMC analysis of the equipment. This paper deals with the detailed analysis of a Car Deck player. The Near Field Emissions from the PCB of a car Deck player was investigated within the frequency range from 9 KHz to 3 GHz. This test was performed from 9 KHz to 30 MHz by an Agilent Close Field Probe HP11941 A at DIT, Pimpri and from 30 MHz to 3 GHz by EMC Precision Scan Tool at ARAI, Pune. All of the measured radiations were plotted using MATLAB. In the near field, E and H fields are separated. The estimation of E field is necessary to compare near field radiations with the automotive standard CISPR 25. Hence E field, H field and Power Density are estimated from the measured near field radiations. The comparison between E field and CISPR 25 standard is plotted in MATLAB which shows that the level of E field is far above the specified standard limit. Shielding methodology is proposed to suppress radiation within a specified limit. Shielding materials such as Cu, Al, Mild Steel and Mumetal are selected to decrease the near field radiations. This paper recommends Al as an effective enclosure material to mitigate the near field radiations.

articleTitle: Demystifying Via Impedance Optimization for High Speed Channels
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Signal speeds of high speed channels double almost every generation and with increasing speeds, even a slight impedance discontinuity in the channel can adversely affect signal quality. Channel discontinuities come from several sources and each source must be carefully considered. One common source of channel discontinuity is the signal via. Via impedance needs to be designed with utmost care because high speed channels inevitably encounter a lot of via transitions in the form of BGA breakout vias, AC coupling capacitor vias, connector vias and transition vias. Upfront modeling and analysis for vias can mitigate reflections in a layout to achieve the required performance. In this paper, a method to optimize vias in both time and frequency domains is explained. A lot of common mistakes made in terms of rise-time assumptions, reference impedances and impedance targets are demystified and explained in detail with examples. This paper highlights the impact on via impedance on high frequency designs and showcases how in correct modeling assumptions can lead to suboptimal designs or in unnecessary overdesigning of the channels.

articleTitle: In-Situ Measurements and Simulation Analysis of HIRA UWB System
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Ultra wide band is a radio technology offers very low energy level for short range with very high bandwidth. Impulse Radiating Antennas (IRA) are special class of antennas suited for radiating very fast pulses in a narrow beam. A fast-rising step-like signal fed into the antenna produces an approximate delta-function response in the far field. In the present paper an Insitu measurements of a UWB system with Half Impulse Radiating Antenna (HIRA) installed SAMEER CE3 was presented. The Installed UWB antenna structure and its radiation patterns are simulated using CST 3D EM simulation tool to study & analyze the distribution of EM far fields, radiation pattern and surface currents distribution. The simulation results are verified with practical measurements, and both are in close agreement. This system can be utilized for in situ transient EMP pre-compliance testing to evaluate the equipment against EMP events.

articleTitle: Study of effect of Parasitic on Conducted Emissions from Flyback Converter through Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In every few months we see a new product in market. Today's race of designing a new low cost and feature rich product instantly and readymade solutions from IC manufacturer have limit the knowledge of engineers. Design tools have made the component selection easy but have neglected the parasitic. Simulation tools are also being used to see impact of component tolerances only. Parasitic could not find place in design calculation, schematic and PCB layout but have major impact on EMC performance. This paper describes the modelling of parasitic elements in power supply and prediction of emissions at design level before actual prototype of board.

articleTitle: Firefly Algorithm based Pseudo-Orthogonal codes for reducing sidelobes and electromagnetic interference
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The first criterion for designing an effective radar is its range resolution. Modern radars are utilizing MIMO (Multi Input Multi Output) functionality for high resolution and greater data collection. To support MIMO functionality within the spectral usage requirements and elimination of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) due to multiple wave transition, pseudo-orthogonal code sets are preferable. An analysis of common pulse compression waveforms such as polyphase, LFM and NLFM waveforms for suitability in the pseudo-orthogonal waveform is desirable. For a simultaneous transmit and simultaneous receive operational mode to be realized without sacrificing range resolution, the waveforms being transmitted must be isolated from each other. When calculating the isolation and electromagnetic interference between waveforms, the highest magnitude of the cross-correlation is the determining factor. Indeed, in this paper Firefly Algorithm based Pseud-Orthogonal Code Sets (POCS) are used and compared all the Pseudo-orthogonal code sets PSLR values.

articleTitle: Calculation of Shielding Effectiveness of an Enclosure with Arbitrary Shaped Apertures using Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Calculation of shielding effectiveness (SE) of enclosures with apertures calculated analytically consumes very less time compared with simulating the whole structure using full wave solvers. But aperture impedance is available only for few shapes in literatures. In this paper, SE is computed using the transmission line approach combined with fullwave simulation. Impedance of arbitrary shaped aperture is calculated using full wave simulation which requires very less time and it is combined with transmission line approach to calculate SE of enclosure. This approach can be extended to enclosures with array of apertures and multiple layers of apertures. The whole enclosure with aperture is simulated, and the results are matching with SE computed using this time efficient hybrid approach.

articleTitle: Differences Between Standard Deviation and Robust NIQR Method During Z-Score Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper presents and analyzes the differences between two different statistical methods, in determining Zscore during Interlaboratory comparison of Radiated Emission measurement. The Z-score results determined using standard deviation method were compared with Robust Normalized Inter Quartile Range method. Proficiency Testing and Interlaboratory comparison measurements are mandatory requirements for Testing and calibration Laboratories as per clause 5.9 of ISO/IEC 17025 [1] accreditation. The Testing laboratories having their test setup complying to RTCA DO160G [2] standard was chosen for the Interlaboratory comparison programme. The results of each participating laboratories were statistically analyzed as described in ISO/IEC 17043 [3] and ISO 13528 [4] standard.

articleTitle: Modeling & Simulation Analysis of Frequency Selective Fabrics (FSF) for evaluation of its Shielding Effectiveness in GSM band
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Frequency selective surface (FSS) is a repeated structure which can transmit, reflect or absorb the incident electromagnetic wave based up on the application interest using patches or slots. The patch and slot arrays effectively create band stop and band pass filters. The FSS have potential applications in providing sufficient Shielding in the desired frequency ranges. The work proposed in this paper is to study & analyze the FSS structural requirements to shield against the GSM band frequencies. The persons working near the mobile towers are exposed to strong EM fields, hence they need to guard themselves against these fields. The concept of FSS is extended to print the structures on the plane fabrics, and the same can be worn by the working personnel. The paper is primarily based on the simulation analysis of the designed fabrics using EM software tools. The simulation results are validated using experimental results.

articleTitle: MMF Analysis of Polyphase sequences for EMI suppression using Cyclic Algorithm-Pruned
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Most of the RADAR and Telecommunication system are affected by EMI. In the past, frequency allocation to different frequency bands can minimize the EMI and narrow bandwidth usage. EMI reduction requires other means than frequency allocation possibly non-interfering coded waveforms or sequences such as PI, P2, P3, P4, Px, Golomb, Frank, and the Chu known as Polyphase sequences. The commonly used waveforms in RADAR are frequency phase and amplitude. In this paper, the Modified Merit Factor (MMF) and minimum correlation level are used as the parameters to analyze the EMI reduction in RADAR. Weighted Integrated sidelobe level (WISL) metric can reduce the correlation level for a region of interest. Out of Cyclic Algorithm pruned obtained Polyphase sequences CAP (Chu), CAP (Px) and CAP (Golomb) exhibit the minimum correlation level as -81.77dB, 132. 77dB and 155. 15dB for Lengths $10^{2}, 10^{3}$ and $10^{4}$ respectively. These sequences are more immune to interference. All the results are implemented on MATLAB.

articleTitle: Calibration requirements for impulse magnetic field immunity test system as per IEC 61000-4-9 standard
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The IEC 61000-4-9:2016 standard is used to demonstrate the immunity of electrical and electronic equipment when subjected to impulse magnetic fields due to switching and lightning effects. This paper describes the calibration of test generator and test system as per IEC 61000-4-9 Edition 2 standard. This paper also discusses about the significant differences between the IEC 61000-4-9 edition 1 and edition 2 standards with emphasis on calibration of test system/test levels.

articleTitle: Reduction of Radiated Emission from Offline Switch Mode Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Switch Mode Power Supply (SMPS) loads are intensifying as the electronics industry requires more DC-DC conversion. The ElectroMagnetic Interference (EMI) generated from the DC-DC converter effects the performance of integrated circuits which receive power supply. Because of high frequency switching of the semiconductor, ringing waveforms are observed and this causes increase in radiation emission. In this paper a RC snubber circuit can be used in parallel with the semiconductor switch of the SMPS to reduce unwanted distortion and ringing on the output waveform. This can be above the stipulated limits of EMC regulations of international standards. This is investigated for buck and boost converter converter. The frequency ranges of emissions are measured. This ringing is reduced by proper snubber circuit design. The range of frequencies emitted by this ringing waveform is found from simulation studies and its radiation at a 10m distance is calculated by mathematical formulae. The maximum PCB trace length that can be used in fabricating such SMPS circuits is presented which may help in reducing the radiated emissions at the design stage.

articleTitle: NASA ISRO Synthetic Aperture RADAR (NISAR) Spacecraft Electric Field Studies
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The objective of this analysis is to derive radiation susceptibility levels for subsystems in the NASA ISRO Synthetic Aperture RADAR (NISAR) Spacecraft at Sband SAR payload frequency. This involves finding electromagnetic field distribution at various subsystem locations. The analysis was carried using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) microwave studio software. In Microwave studio Time Domain Solver with Finite Integration Technique (FIT) is used to find out the Electric field distribution at various panels of the spacecraft.

articleTitle: Validation of Anechoic Chamber for Radiated Emission Test
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Radiated emissions testing involve measuring the electromagnetic field strength of the emissions from the EUT and associated cables. To avoid interference from ambient signal of radio and other emitter in populated area, with the measurement, an anechoic chamber is essentially required. During testing, the ambient electromagnetic level in an anechoic chamber measured with the EUT de-energized and all auxiliary equipment turned on, shall be at least 6dB below the allowable specified limits when tests are performed in the chamber. Sometimes this ambient level is not achieved. This paper describes practical techniques applied for ensuring compliance with the ambient requirements for Radiated emission test as per MIL-STD 461. It also discussed the shielding effectiveness of the chamber.

articleTitle: Factors Affecting Near-End Crosstalk (NEXT) in High Speed Serial Links
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, factors affecting near-end crosstalk (NEXT) in high speed serial links are discussed. When designing stripline transmission lines, care should be taken to tune parameters such as dielectric thickness of core and prepreg, intra-pair spacing and pair-to-pair spacing to minimize crosstalk. A less optimal design would result in higher crosstalk and may force designers to increase layer count in printed circuit boards (PCB) to reduce crosstalk. In this paper, by comparing eye-height differences between high speed channels with and without NEXT, the sensitivity of different transmission line parameters to NEXT is analyzed.

articleTitle: Enhancement of PCB Design for Radiated Immunity Compliance in Analog Signal Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: As Electronic industry is progressing through the decades, electronic products tend to become increasingly complex. One of the major challenges in the industry today is to design products with Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) in the given size and cost. In order to ensure a certain product meets global norms related to Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) and EMC there are specific standards which a product has to comply. Such a challenging standard is IEC61000-4-3 which is the International Standard for Radiated, Radio Frequency, and Electromagnetic field immunity test. Radiated immunity is especially demanding in products without a metal body, polycarbonate or other plastics provide no shielding against electromagnetic radiation. Due to constraints in size and cost the PCB design should be optimum so as to provide maximum immunity against radiation. Very low power analog signals are highly susceptible to radiated noise, operational amplifier circuits malfunction if susceptible to radiation. In this research work various improvements done in the PCB design of the operational amplifier section to achieve radiated immunity in a previously non complaint design is shown.

articleTitle: Performance of single and double layered wire mesh electromagnetic shield(s) in the laboratories of degree engineering colleges
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is a disturbance generated by an external source that affects electronic and electrical circuits either by conduction or by electromagnetic radiation. The disturbance may degrade the performance of the circuits or even stop it from functioning. To protect the victims from radiated EMI electromagnetic shielding is necessary. The authors of this paper have tried to present an analysis on the design approach of perforated shields working in the X band (8GHz-12GHz),made of different materials like (i) only Cu, (ii) only Stainless Steel and (iii) combination of Cu and stainless steel(both single and double layered) by changing the distance between the victim and the shield. The shield is also rotated around an axis perpendicular to the horizon. To achieve better effectiveness and reduction in mass perforated or wire mesh shields are the best solution. The plane of the shields ware always kept perpendicular to the plane of the test bench (i.e. the horizon). Due to perforation the shields became less costly, though caused acceptable and considerable shielding effectiveness. Authors of this paper have tried to offer a course solution at low cost against the ill-effects of EMI, active inside any Antenna and Microwave laboratories of degree Engineering Colleges.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a 1−18 GHz Double-Ridged Horn Antenna with Improved Patterns
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, the design and development of a broad-band double ridge horn antenna (DRHA) have been presented. From the throat to the aperture, the ridge is tapered for smooth impedance matching between the waveguide section and the free-space. A linear taper superimposed on an exponential taper has been conceived in the flared horn section. The additional linear taper reduces the aperture phase error and yields improved patterns at higher frequencies. Design optimizations have been carried out using finite element based high frequency structure simulator (HFSS). A prototype has been fabricated using aluminum and experimentally validated. Relevant simulation and experimental results are also presented.

articleTitle: CM Noise Cancellation in Near Unity Power Factor Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: NUPF (Near Unity Power Factor) converter can improve the low power factor offered by offline SMPS. But, the NUPF also generate EMI which needs to be mitigated to comply with EMC standards. This paper provides an approach to minimize CM (Common Mode) conducted EMI noise by cancellation technique. Here an extra winding PCW (Parasitic capacitance noise Cancellation Winding) in the high-frequency transformer is used to reduce the common mode conducted EMI. By this method, the high-frequency range of CM noise reduction has been achieved and it can reduce the cost of the EMI filter. Experimentation and simulation are carried out with and without PCW for a 30W flyback NUPF and a significant reduction in high-frequency CM conducted EMI is obtained.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Unintentional Radiated Emission Caused by Thermal Glue used in Products with Metal Enclosure
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: It is quite common to use heat towers for thermal management for industrial grade electronic products with metal enclosure. Thermal glue or thermal tape is used between a high heat dissipating Integrated Circuit (IC) and corresponding heat tower to facilitate proper heat transfer from the IC to the metal enclosure. Though these heat towers and thermal glue are essential for passing temperature compliance test, they can cause serious high frequency emission issues which can fail Radiated Emission (RE) test. This paper reports the effect of thermal glue on RE test results of an industrial product with metal enclosure and suggests ways to mitigate them.

articleTitle: Survey on Biological Effects of Mobile Phone Radiation, Measurement Techniques and Radiation Shields
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Microwaves are widely used in many applications. This made it possible for continent to continent communication. With this, one can reach the unreachable location by other means. Mobile phone communication is the marked field. This gives more freedom to the user to be anywhere and anytime. The advancements in the field of wireless technology in terms of sophistication and price reduction, made many to use the wireless products such as Mobile phone, Blue-tooth, Wi-Fi, etc., One of the important facets of this ubiquitous technology is the risk associated with this. It increases the interaction of electromagnetic fields radiation with the biological tissues of plants, animals and humans. This microwave affects biological ells in two ways, Thermal and Non-thermal. This persuades researchers to study the pros and cons of this inevitable technology. This paper reviews some of the vital studies which concluded the ill-effects of using Mobile-phone, some of the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) measurement techniques, techniques to reduce the radiation levels and the significance of a new class material, a material which was the advent of 21st century i.e., Meta material in electromagnetic(EM) radiation reduction are presented.

articleTitle: The Near Electric Field Produced by a Wireless Power Transfer System Employing DD Polarized Couplers
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The intense near magnetic field associated with inductive wireless power transfer has been studied extensively. However, the near electric field of such a system can also be intense and has received much less attention. We provide an exposition of the near electric field for the DD coupler as described in the SAE J2954 TIR. Simulations and experimental data are presented. Some effort has been taken to reconcile the numerically-simulated and measured data as the measured data for the electric field necessarily reflects the non-ideal characteristics of a finite-sized probe.

articleTitle: Study of feasibility of Enhancement of cable length for surge immunity test
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: High energy surge pulse of specific profile is injected for evaluation compatibility. Signal integrity requires a frequency response of cable adequate for signal transmission. Pulse rise time is the indicator for the adequacy of cable bandwidth. Cable longer than specified length may be used if pulse profile remains undisturbed.

articleTitle: T-shaped Broadband CPW - fed Folded-Slot Antenna for 5.8 GHz RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: A novel design of T-shaped broadband CoPlanar Waveguide (CPW) - fed folded slot monopole antenna is proposed for the application of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) at 5.8 GHz. The proposed antenna is fabricated on FR-4 substrate and having the size of 16.5 mm x 20 mm. The bandwidth of 30.17% and peak antenna gain of more than 4.15 dBi has been achieved from the proposed antenna through simulation and testing. The fundamental parameters of antenna which meets the acceptable standards are measured. The radiation pattern of broadside and bidirectional in E-Plane and omni directional in H plane are also observed.

articleTitle: Technical Competence in Design, Simulation & Validation of India’s Largest outdoor RS105 facility
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) is a short burst of electromagnetic energy which can disrupt the electrical & electronic systems. There is a need for the electronic Systems to comply with the levels of EMP produced as per MIL STD 461 F/G, RS105. The communication, defense and now extended to civilian sectors are major victims for the electromagnetic pulse. This paper mainly focuses on technical competence in realizing India's Largest Outdoor RS105 Test Facility. Design of Electrical Ground plane and Modeling & Simulation analysis of bounded wave EMP antenna was carried out to verify the field uniformity as per the standard. System was commissioned and validated to meet the compliance testing for RS105 as per the MIL standards with generated test levels more than 50 kV/m and covering the EUT test volume of 17m(L)×12m(W)×3m(H), sufficient to test the large defense and civilian systems. Facility opened for serving the Indian industries.

articleTitle: EMC design modifications to solve field failure due to ESD - A case study
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: One of the major challenges faced by the electronic product designers is to qualify their product for Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) phenomena. This paper discusses a case study of ESD phenomena and recurrent field failures in a consumer electronics product and the solution to the problem. In this paper, the circuit level EMC design modifications that were suggested / implemented to improve the immunity of the product to static electricity discharges are presented. In addition, techniques of shielding the PCB, found necessary to improve the ESD immunity of the product for radiated ESD events, are also presented.

articleTitle: Absolute Charging Estimation of Spacecraft in Severe GEO Plasma Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: This article presents the evaluation of capacitance matrix and transient variation of body potential of a satellite modeled as a metallic (Aluminum) structure consisting of a cuboid with two coplanar rectangular plates. The capacitance required for the estimation of body potential is evaluated using the Method of Moments. The impact of the coupled body capacitance in the transient profile of body potential is carried out with reference to that of the isolated bodies. Owing to well-known fact that diverse secondary and backscattered electron yield for different materials is the prime reason for the most destructive differential charging, this work presents its impact for the normal and isotropic incidence of primary particles, which results into a significant amendment in the estimation of absolute charging reported earlier. Absolute charging analysis of a satellite is presented in the normal and worst cases of single Maxwellian plasma environment. The validity of the charging analysis is established with that available in the open literature.

articleTitle: EMC Considerations in Designing RF Modules for E/F Band Exciter
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper emphasizes on EMI/EMC design considerations that are implemented in the up converter and local oscillator (LO) modules in E/F Band Exciter. The up converted waveform is fed to the dual transmit receive unit for transmitting through radiating elements and LO's to receiver unit of the Radar. This up converter system receives 60MHz modulated IF and up converts to UHF frequency in 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> up conversion and in the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> up conversion to E/F band with the help of two local oscillators. EMI /EMC issues have been treated in this work by considering design, PCB layout, components selection, distribution of power supply and housing.

articleTitle: Conducted interference on electron gun power supplies of DC EB accelerator
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Internal electromagnetic interference produced by a 3MeV, 10mA industrial electron beam accelerator is presented in this paper. Accelerating potential for this accelerator is generated by a parallel coupled voltage multiplier based high voltage power supply. Electron beam is produced by an electron gun using a thermionic emitter. The electron gun, which is located at the high voltage terminal of the accelerator, has to be powered by isolated power supplies floating at the accelerating potential in the order of 3MV. Operating power for the power supplies are extracted from the multiplier column itself. At full terminal voltage, 1000J energy is stored in the terminal capacitance. During occasional electrical breakdowns in the system, the stored energy is released creating high frequency, high current transients in the frequency range of several MHz. The floating power supplies are subjected to severe electromagnetic interference during the discharges. This paper describes some of the identified breakdown pathways, estimation of associated conducted stresses on the power supplies and protection methods.

articleTitle: Modeling & Simulation Analysis for evaluation of Electromagnetic Sheilding Effectiveness of Conductive Fabrics using Flanged Co-axial Transmission Line Holder as per ASTM D4935-10 standard
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In recent years, Conductive Fabrics have been enormous demand in variety of applications which includes defense, industry, aircraft, wireless communication and consumer sectors. The conductive fabrics offers shielding against the intentional & un-intentional electromagnetic radiations. In this paper, we modelled the (FCTLH) as per ASTM D4935-10 Standard to measure the Shielding Effectiveness (SE) of planar materials. Altair Hyper Works FEKO simulation software is used to model the CTLH and evaluated the S-parameters and VSWR. Four samples made from different material compositions are modeled in the software and computed the shielding effectiveness of these planar samples as per the standard.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Coplanar Waveguide Antenna With Single Frequency Notch
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: An ultra wideband slot antenna using coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed is proposed in this letter. The antenna consists of a hexagonal shaped ground slot and a rectangular radiating patch. Hexagonal ground plane provides a gradual variation in slot impedance due to tapered sections, resulting in wideband nature. The radiating patch is loaded with two notches accounting for ultra wideband nature. A metallic arm is embedded in the ground plane and is protruded into the hexagonal slot resulting in a frequency notch, thereby providing frequency isolation between WiMAX and WLAN band. The proposed antenna operates for entire ultra wideband range with rejecting the frequency band extending from 4.05GHz - 5.4GHz.

articleTitle: Low cost Verification method for PC based Harmonics Power Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of a simple and low cost method to analyze the performance of harmonics emission measurement system in real time as per IEC 61000-3-2 standard. A Harmonics frequency generator (HFG) was designed and developed for this purpose. The proposed technique may be a useful alternative method for calibration/verification of PC based harmonics power analyzer.

articleTitle: Use of Simulation in EMC optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: EMC engineers should be involved in the product design process right from the initial stages in order to ensure effective product compliance. But, when electromagnetic compliance is not considered until the last stages, troubleshooting using measurement can only happen at the end which poses a limitation for layout modification. Simulation can help this process as it can be done at an earlier stage and used to predict the necessary layout changes. This can then be validated by measurement when the prototype is available. The objective of this paper is to draw a comparison between simulation and measurement and to show that simulation can help in the design cycle by saving cost and time.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Critical Point-of-entry (POE) protection devices for E1 & E2 pulses as per MIL STD 188-125-1&2
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: High-Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP) is a severe threat to the electronics across wide sectors viz. commercial, industrial, defense, etc. The electronics which are operating to perform critical, time-urgent command, control, communications, computer, and intelligence (C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I) missions for hardening of HEMP need to be evaluated for the pulses as per MIL STD 188-125-1&2. In this paper, various types of point-of-entry (POE) protection systems are evaluated for E1 & E2 HEMP pulses by measuring the residual currents.

articleTitle: Analysis of Horn Antenna calibration as per SAE ARP958D Standard and three antenna method prescribed by ANSI C63.5 standard
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: EMC antennas need to be calibrated for the parameter Antenna Factor (AF). In the radiated emission measurement, Antenna Factor shall be added to the EMI receiver reading to obtain the emission level which will be compared with the limit lines prescribed in the EMC standards. The radiated emission (RE102) measurement as per MIL STD 461E/F/G is carried out at 1m distance. Hence the Antenna Factor at 1m distance is required to calculate the emission level. SAE ARP 958D “Electromagnetic Interference Measurement Antennas; Standard calibration method” is the standard which provides the procedures for calibration of the antennas at 1m distance.ANSI C64.5 is an another standard which provides calibration of antennas at 10m(up to 1.0GHz) and 3m (for 1GHz and above) distances. This paper analyzes SAE ARP 958D method and its associated discrepancies for the horn antenna calibration. This paper also discusses about a calibration method based on the ANSI C63.5 STD and its results obtained for the horn antenna calibration.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Transmission Line Model for Predicting the Electromagnetic Interference Suppression Characteristics of Ferrite cores
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In this paper, an equivalent transmission line model (TLM) is proposed for predicting the suppression characteristics of ferrite cores by making use of their material characteristics provided by the manufacturers. The effect of increasing the number of turns of wire, wound around the core is also evaluated. A test jig is fabricated to validate the model. Experiments are performed using the test jig and the scattering parameters are measured from 100 kHz to 100 MHz. In addition, a square wave, which is a common noise waveform in digital platforms, is applied to the jig and the suppression level is measured to verify the competence of the proposed model for its real-time application. It is found that the results obtained from the measurements are in good agreement with the predicted responses in both the experiments.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge Test On Fuzes as per MIL-STD-331C
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Fuze and its electronics has to encounter high levels of Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) during its lifetime. Fuzes are subjected to Personnel borne and Helicoptor borne ESD as per MIL-STD-331C. This paper outlines the testing measurement techniques for the test F1.2 Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) in MIL STD 331C standard.

articleTitle: Magnetic Compatibility Studies of Bus Bar and Magnetic Torquer in GSAT-19
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: In GSAT-19 spacecraft, one of the magnetic torquer is located very near to the bus bar. The objective of this study is to estimate the DC magnetic field generated by bus bar at magnetic torquer location and verify the magnetic compatibility between busbar and torquer. The modelling and simulation are carried out with the help of Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software. Magneto static solver [3] is used to find out the Magnetic field at magnetic torquer location in spacecraft. The magnetic field values estimated from the simulations are compared with the experimentally measured values.

articleTitle: Design of Bounded Wave NEMP (RS105) Test Simulator
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Nuclear EMP destroys power grids electronic systems, communication. NEMP hardness is essentially required to be incorporated in systems during design itself. NEMP RS105 Test as per MIL-STD 461E/F is conducted on the systems to achieve desired level of confidence that the systems are designed and implemented for NEMP Hardness. NEMP Test system consists of EMP Simulator for simulation of NEMP Pulse. The paper describes the various test simulators used for conduct of NEMP RS105 Test as per MIL-STD 461E/F. It brings out the advantages of bounded wave simulator over radiating type.

articleTitle: A Mixed E-B Finite Element Formulation for the analysis of Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The analysis of periodic structures with the Finite Element Method (FEM) has received a lot of attention in recent years. FEM formulates Maxwell's curl equations as either a second-order wave equation or two dual first-order (mixed) equations. Up until now the analysis of the periodic structures was primarily restricted to using the second-order wave equation. In this work, a new mixed vector finite element method for solving the coupled Maxwell's equations for the periodic boundary condition is presented. The mixed-order formulation gives a higher accuracy compared to the second-order for the same number of mesh elements. Numerical experiments are performed to validate the new formulation with analytical and commercial methods.

articleTitle: Analysis, Simulation and Realization of EM Compatible Rectangular Mobile Enclosure
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Majority of Defense Systems utilizes rectangular enclosures and shelters in mobile systems for carrying various equipment such as communication, surveillance, CBRN sensors, power supplies etc. The electromagnetic compatibility at sub-system level as well as at system level of such equipment is necessary in view of the operational conditions as defined in various military standards. The overall electromagnetic compatibility depends on shielding effectiveness of enclosure used in such systems. The effects of external electromagnetic interferences due to various sources, its coupling to subsystems needs to be under control. Emission control is desired depending upon the deployment and operational requirements. One such fully EM compatible rectangular enclosure is designed and developed. The analysis, simulation and test results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Horn Antenna calibration as per SAE ARP958D Standard and three antenna method prescribed by ANSI C63.5 standard
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: EMC antennas need to be calibrated for the parameter Antenna Factor (AF). articleTitle: Hardware-Simulation Correlation of BCI failures in Capacitive Touch Sensing Application using ICIM
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: Capacitive touch sensors are gaining in popularity as a preferred human machine interface. Ensuring proper functionality of such systems in the presence of conducted electromagnetic interference is a design challenge. The Bulk Current Injection (BCI) method is widely used for such RF immunity testing particularly for automotive systems. If detected at a late stage, compliance failures may lead to expensive redesigns and increased time to market. Therefore, there is an urgent need to improve the prediction of BCI failures at the early design cycle. In this work, first, a methodology is proposed to generate an immunity model for the capacitive sensor IC, as a one-time process from DPI and VNA measurements. Then, a BCI simulation methodology is outlined using hybrid electromagnetic and circuit simulation and embedding the generated IC immunity model. A test-board is built and hardware-simulation correlation is performed. Results indicate reasonable accuracy in prediction using the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Matching Network Design for Wideband Power Amplifier Cascaded with Harmonic Suppression Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: When a wideband power amplifier (PA) is cascaded with harmonic suppression filter, transmission zeros of the filter influence the harmonic impedances seen by the transistor. As a result, output power of the module consisting of PA cascaded with filter is not the power of PA reduced by insertion loss of filter (additivity is lost). This anomaly can be corrected by incorporating harmonic termination mechanism in conventional constant Q matching network. Modified matching network designed by this method retains its harmonic impedance when cascaded with harmonic suppression filter. Design has been validated by comparing performance of PA designed with constant Q matching network and modified matching network. PA with conventional matching network shows 1.5dB drop in power at centre of frequency band after cascading with harmonic suppression filter of 0.6dB insertion loss whereas, PA with the modified matching network shows 0.6dB drop in power at higher edge of band (and lesser at lower edge) after cascading with harmonic suppression filter. Besides restoring the desired additivity when cascaded with filter, this matching network also acts as an integrated harmonic suppression filter. The designed amplifier and filter have been implemented in 73×38 sq.mm and 49×37 sq.mm planar microstrip technology respectively and hence can be seamlessly integrated in compact man-pack radios. Fabricated module consisting of PA and filter delivers 50W power and achieves harmonic power level as low as 80dBc.

publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Conference on ElectroMagnetic Interference & Compatibility (INCEMIC)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: electromagnetic compatibility; electromagnetic interference; calibration; electromagnetic shielding; IEC standards; electromagnetic pulse; immunity testing; printed circuit design; antenna radiation patterns; microwave antennas.
